finding_key: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/pptx-actions.ts::new pptx export fetches attacker-controllable image `src` values with `credentials: "include"` and no scheme/host allowlist
evidence: The code facts in the claim check out: `exportSlidesPptxAndDownload` (pptx-actions.ts:88-100) wires `fetchImage: (src) => docsImageFetcher(src)`, `exportPptx` pre-scans and calls `fetchImage` for every unique `ImageElement.data.src` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts, Step 1/2), `docsImageFetcher` does `fetch(resolved, { credentials: "include" })` (export-utils.ts), and `resolveImageUrl` returns any URL that begins with a scheme untouched — so there is no scheme/host allowlist. The write boundary does allow arbitrary srcs: `assertValidElement` in docs-content.controller.ts only checks `id`/`type`/`frame`, never `data.src`. So the described condition is genuinely present. Impact is modest, though: cross-origin `credentials:'include'` sends only the *target* origin's cookies (no Wafflebase session leak), CORS blocks reading responses so internal probing is mostly timing/error-based, the requester must already be an authorized workspace collaborator, and the editor's canvas renderer already loads the same `src` into an `` (so the IP/UA beacon exists before export). The PDF export path uses the identical fetcher, so this is a pre-existing pattern that the change merely adds another consumer to.
